variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Mix sources for independent evidence”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Domain experts
pairs.detail: Experts can produce and judge nuanced, high-consequence answers.
pairs.explanation: Experts can produce and judge nuanced, high-consequence answers. They are expensive, may share the same institutional assumptions, and still need calibrated rubrics and adjudication.

pairs.label: Trained contributors
pairs.detail: Crowd or internal contributors can add language, style, and scenario breadth.
pairs.explanation: Crowd or internal contributors can add language, style, and scenario breadth. Qualification tests, hidden gold tasks, agreement monitoring, and clear escalation paths are essential.

pairs.label: Synthetic candidates
pairs.detail: Models can generate variations, adversarial cases, and rare formats cheaply.
pairs.explanation: Models can generate variations, adversarial cases, and rare formats cheaply. Their outputs are candidates, not independent truth, and must retain generator and prompt lineage.

variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Domain experts: Experts can produce and judge nuanced, high-consequence answers. Trained contributors: Crowd or internal contributors can add language, style, and scenario breadth. Synthetic candidates: Models can generate variations, adversarial cases, and rare formats cheaply.

pairs.label: Dataset evidence
pairs.detail: Measure schema validity, provenance, duplicates, reviewer agreement, quality dimensions, coverage cells, privacy findings, and split leakage.
pairs.explanation: Measure schema validity, provenance, duplicates, reviewer agreement, quality dimensions, coverage cells, privacy findings, and split leakage.

pairs.label: Model evidence
pairs.detail: Measure task success, safety, calibration where relevant, refusal behavior, regressions, memorization, latency, and critical slices against a frozen baseline.
pairs.explanation: Measure task success, safety, calibration where relevant, refusal behavior, regressions, memorization, latency, and critical slices against a frozen baseline.

pairs.label: Causal evidence
pairs.detail: Run ablations by source, slice, and curation rule.
pairs.explanation: Run ablations by source, slice, and curation rule. Correlation between a larger dataset and a better model does not identify which examples created the gain.

pairs.label: Operational evidence
pairs.detail: Verify access controls, reproducibility, approval history, retention, incident response, rollback, and the ability to delete affected records and derived artifacts.
pairs.explanation: Verify access controls, reproducibility, approval history, retention, incident response, rollback, and the ability to delete affected records and derived artifacts.

Causal evidence: Run ablations by source, slice, and curation rule. variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Demonstration data is a collection of examples that shows a model how to respond: an input or instruction paired with a desired output. Curation is the controlled process of defining, collecting, reviewing, balancing, versioning, and releasing those examples.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Design for curation failures”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Reward hacking the rubric
pairs.detail: Contributors learn surface patterns that score well without satisfying the behavior.
pairs.explanation: Contributors learn surface patterns that score well without satisfying the behavior. Rotate hidden gold tasks, inspect rationales, and measure model outcomes beyond rubric completion.

pairs.label: Synthetic feedback loop
pairs.detail: A model generates, scores, and filters its own patterns until errors look consistent.
pairs.explanation: A model generates, scores, and filters its own patterns until errors look consistent. Keep independent human and external evidence in both review and evaluation.

pairs.label: Coverage theater
pairs.detail: Marginal totals look balanced while critical intersections remain empty.
pairs.explanation: Marginal totals look balanced while critical intersections remain empty. Gate named slice combinations and publish the matrix with the release.

pairs.label: Unrecoverable lineage
pairs.detail: The team cannot identify licensed, private, or deleted material after training.
pairs.explanation: The team cannot identify licensed, private, or deleted material after training. Hash and version records, transformations, splits, checkpoints, and derived models.
